code/rust/core_contracts/src/validation_: Explicit placeholder manifest names a sample nonexistent-by-contract subject rather than a generated workspace census. Admission checks nonempty header/parts, at least one required part, nonzero schema-hash bytes, unique part names and trait_impl/contract kind presence for BaseType. It does not read a file, hash its schema, require validator presence, check authority or enforce known kinds for other subjects. Tests cover the sample's three metadata parts and all-zero hash refusal. This is placeholder metadata validation, not completed contract generation or source audit.

Erased-validator interface and descriptor admission check only EvidenceOnly label and unique IDs. Empty batches and a single blank ID are accepted; subject type, property and zero schema hashes are not validated, as the tests explicitly use zero hashes. No registry lookup implementation or evidence execution occurs here. Tests cover a two-item batch and duplicate ID; structural descriptor admission does not certify a validator's behavior.

Defines public serializable status/decision labels and a private ObligationTally that refuses failed>checked then deterministically prioritizes domain fault, failures, positive checked success, and zero-check indeterminate. Tests exercise all four classifications and inconsistent counts. This is a sound finite count classifier but consumes declared counts without individual obligation identities or predicate execution; Valid is not an independent universal invariant proof.

Validator is a public implementable trait with an overrideable EvidenceOnly default and caller-associated witness/violation types. The ten forbidden capabilities are declaration metadata. ValidatorFence checks a supplied capability list is exactly the unique ten static entries using checked counters and stores the count; it neither inspects validator code nor constrains its side effects. Tests cover exact list, empty list and wrong count. The fence certifies list equality, not runtime inability to execute forbidden operations.

Public serializable result/artifact records carry caller witnesses/violations, duplicated status and metadata. Constructor derives status and EvidenceOnly and hashes framed identity fields/status with BLAKE3; witness/violation payload and authority effect are omitted from the hash, and public fields allow later inconsistency. No verifier recomputes the digest or evaluates evidence here. Shared capacity tests alone occur locally. Artifact hash is an identity/status digest rather than a commitment to the complete validation evidence.

Defines a serializable erased violation trait and a private positive absolute u64 gap record. Constructor rejects an empty code and equal expected/observed counts using checked subtraction, but retains only gap, dropping the code, original counts and direction. Tests cover gap5 and equality refusal plus capacity template. This is finite arithmetic consistency, not a binding to an observed artifact or a specific violated predicate.

FileValidator is a declaration-only interface over a caller-supplied path/kind/schema/parts record. admit_parts checks nonempty header and part name/kind, unique names, and checked required/optional partition counts, permitting an empty parts list. It never reads source or checks schema/authority; tests intentionally use a zero schema hash and validate counting/duplicate refusal. The result is a census of declared parts, not evidence that required source parts exist or were substantively reviewed.

Assertion helper panics on empty identity fields, non-EvidenceOnly label, empty result evidence and witness-property mismatch. It does not compare stored status with result.status, verify schema/hash grammar, recompute artifact_hash or inspect evidence semantics. ArtifactFieldCensus merely requires seven arbitrary nonempty strings and checked count7. Its small tests and shared capacity template do not establish artifact authenticity or semantic validity.
code/rust/core_contracts/src/enforcement: Generated law inventory is explicitly empty. Public GeneratedLawCensus::try_generated therefore accepts only an empty claim, while try_against compares two caller-provided finite inventories for nonempty unique IDs, positive generated clause counts, exact correspondence and checked sum. Tests honestly cover empty generation, invented-law refusal and a sample count mismatch. No laws are generated or executed by this file; inventory agreement is not proof of law validity.

Reexports governance owners and defines a finite proposal classifier: caller-selected Bureau::Blackrod IDs are admitted uniquely, Adversary IDs are counted/refused, and totals use checked u32 arithmetic. No signature, authentication, policy or action is checked here despite the signed-bureau wording; duplicate adversary findings can be counted. Tests exercise bureau distinction and duplicate admitted ID. Categorical functor and real-world safety statements are architectural intentions requiring concrete owners, not established by this count partition.
